facts.fact: According to Nielsen's The Gauge, streaming held 47.6% of all U.S. TV viewing in April 2026.
facts.quote: In April 2026, streaming took **47.6% of all U.S. TV viewing while cable held just 21.6%**, according to Nielsen's The Gauge.

facts.fact: According to Nielsen's The Gauge, broadcast held 19.9% of U.S. TV viewing in April 2026.
facts.quote: **Broadcast:** 19.9%

facts.fact: According to Nielsen's The Gauge, the 'Other' category (gaming, physical media, unmeasured tuning) held 10.9% of U.S. TV viewing in April 2026.
facts.quote: **Other (gaming, physical media, unmeasured tuning):** 10.9%

facts.fact: In April 2026, streaming's 47.6% share was more than cable and broadcast combined, which together came to 41.5%.
facts.quote: Streaming's 47.6% is more than cable and broadcast combined, which together came to 41.5%.

facts.fact: Streaming first exceeded combined broadcast and cable viewing in Nielsen data in May 2025.
facts.quote: That crossover, streaming beating all of traditional TV at once, [first happened in May 2025]

facts.fact: Cable's share rose to 21.6% in April 2026, a six-month high, driven by live sports.
facts.quote: Cable ticked up to 21.6% in April, a six-month high, on the strength of live sports like the NCAA championship

facts.fact: Nielsen data shows streaming's share of U.S. TV viewing rose from 44.3% in April 2025 to 47.6% in April 2026, a gain of 3.3 points.
facts.quote: **Streaming:** 44.3% to 47.6%, a gain of 3.3 points

facts.fact: Nielsen data shows cable's share of U.S. TV viewing fell from 24.5% in April 2025 to 21.6% in April 2026, a loss of 2.9 points.
facts.quote: **Cable:** 24.5% to 21.6%, a loss of 2.9 points

facts.fact: Nielsen data shows broadcast's share of U.S. TV viewing fell from 20.8% in April 2025 to 19.9% in April 2026, a loss of 0.9 points.
facts.quote: **Broadcast:** 20.8% to 19.9%, a loss of 0.9 points

facts.fact: The gap between streaming and cable viewing share in April 2026 was about 26 percentage points.
facts.quote: That's a gap of about 26 percentage points between the two.

facts.fact: Nielsen's April 2026 Gauge report was released June 25, 2026.
facts.quote: The [April 2026 report](https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2026/sports-and-dramas-drive-april-viewing-patterns-in-nielsens-latest-gauge-reports/), released June 25, 2026, is the freshest complete picture

facts.fact: Nielsen delayed its March 2026 Gauge report amid a dispute over a new measurement methodology.
facts.quote: Nielsen delayed its March Gauge amid a dispute over new measurement methodology, and the recalibrated version isn't expected until the fall.

facts.fact: According to a September 23, 2026 update on the page, Nielsen reported streaming at 49.0% and cable at 18.7% for July 2026.
facts.quote: including July streaming at 49.0% and cable at 18.7%
